A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 100. This would result from forgetting to convert $100 \text{km h}^{-1}$ to $\text{m s}^{-1}$ correctly or misplacing powers of 10.

B.explanation: Gives $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \approx 2.3 \times 10^8 \text{ J}$, whose nearest power of 10 is $10^8 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: Too large by a factor of about 100. This would result from using $v = 100 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ instead of converting $100 \text{km h}^{-1}$ to about $28 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Far too large. This would result from using $m = 600000 \text{ g}$ or squaring incorrectly and overestimating $v^2$ by several powers of 10.

hints: Notice the speed is given as $100 \text{km h}^{-1}$ but kinetic energy needs $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ - divide by $3.6$ to get about $28 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall kinetic energy is $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ with $m = 6.0 \times 10^5 \text{ kg}$, so the $v^2$ term near $10^3$ will dominate the size of the answer.
Estimate $0.5 \times 6 \times 10^5 \times (3 \times 10^1)^2$ and decide which power $10^6$, $10^8$, $10^{10}$ or $10^{12}$ it is closest to.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $m = 600000 \text{ kg} = 6.0 \times 10^5 \text{ kg}$ and $v = 100 \text{km h}^{-1}$.
Convert speed to SI units: $v = 100 \times 1000 / 3600 \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 27.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $v \approx 3 \times 10^1 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for an estimate.
State the governing rule: kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$.
Substitute values with units: $E_k \approx 0.5 \times (6.0 \times 10^5 \text{ kg}) \times (27.8 \text{ m s}^{-1})^2$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $(27.8)^2 \approx 773$, so $E_k \approx 3.0 \times 10^5 \times 773 \approx 2.3 \times 10^8 \text{ J}$.
Order of magnitude means nearest power of 10. $2.3 \times 10^8$ is closest to $10^8 \text{ J}$. This is option B.
